questions.text: What is the most source-safe first step in equipment selection?

options.text: Match the plant to the work method, required output, access, circulation, and maintenance constraints
Select the largest available machine every time
Choose equipment by color
Delay equipment planning until after completion

questions.rationale: Chudley/Greeno links plant decisions to output, transport, site layout, circulation, and hard standing.
questions.explanation: Plate compactors are better for granular soils, not clay. Sheep's foot rollers are for cohesive soils, not asphalt. Equipment characteristics determine suitability; selection by soil type is essential. Soil compaction to required density (90–98%) uses specialized equipment. Sheep's foot rollers with protruding feet are ideal for cohesive (clay) soils: feet penetrate and knead material, achieving density. Plate compactors suit granular (sandy) soils. Smooth drum rollers provide finish work on granular materials and asphalt.
